CORPORATE OVERVIEW MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS STATUTORY REPORTS FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
The landscape of mobility is undergoing a significant shift, driven by changing consumer desires, rapid technical innovation and a growing emphasis on environmental responsibility. The traditional model of vehicle ownership is giving way to a new era of flexible, interconnected, and inclusive transport options. This evolution is not just about the vehicles themselves, but about enhancing the entire journey to make daily commute more efficient and sustainable.
THEME INTRODUCTION FUTURE OF MOBILITY
Hero MotoCorp is at the forefront of this movement, cultivating a comprehensive mobility ecosystem. Our diverse portfolio addresses the needs of every rider, from those seeking mass-market accessibility to premium enthusiasts. A key highlight of our recent innovation is the Glamour X, which stands as the first 125cc motorcycle to feature cruise control technology.
Our commitment to an electric future is reflected in our VIDA brand, where we are building both high-quality vehicles and the essential charging infrastructure required for mass adoption. We have also introduced groundbreaking concepts like DIRT.E K3, India's first modular electric vehicle for young riders, and the Surge S32, which demonstrates our ability to turn visionary ideas into practical applications.

Technical innovation continues to be a fundamental pillar of our over-arching strategy. We launched Novus, a pioneering platform for future mobility dedicated to investigating novel architectures and visionary concepts tailored for changing urban transport ecosystems. Representing our philosophy that "life is movement", the Novus line reflects our ambition to seamlessly merge technology, sustainability and the human experience. Making its global debut at EICMA 2025, the platform showcased three distinct mobility concepts: NEX1, NEX2 and NEX3.
At the core of our digital transformation is our proprietary Connected Vehicle Platform—a robust, scalable ecosystem that bridges manufacturing intelligence with real-world vehicle telemetry. By managing the entire vehicle and customer journey from production to end-of-life, and utilising regular OTA (over the air) updates to keep software updated and capabilities relevant, this platform transforms our vehicles from static products into dynamic, revenue-generating service environments.

Beyond engineering, we are dedicated to creating economic opportunities by supporting the gig economy and empowering micro-entrepreneurs through accessible transport. Throughout these efforts, we maintain a steadfast commitment to sustainability, ensuring responsible waste management and lower emissions across our entire operation. We are committed to a future of mobility that is smarter, cleaner and accessible to all.
We aim to build a future of mobility that is cleaner, smarter and designed for everyone.
VIDA VX2 Plus

EXECUTIVE CHAIRMAN’S MESSAGE
A LEGACY IN MOTION
Our aspiration is clear: To build Hero MotoCorp into one of the world’s most trusted, innovative, and sustainable mobility companies.
Dear Shareholders,

Dear Shareholders,
Our aspiration is clear: to build Hero MotoCorp into one of the world’s most trusted, innovative, and sustainable mobility companies.
In FY 2025-26, Hero MotoCorp further strengthened its position as a global mobility company — guided by purpose, driven by disciplined execution, and anchored in innovation and customer trust.
In this dynamic environment, we are not content to rely solely on our legacy. Instead, we are actively reimagining our future — strengthening our core business, accelerating innovation, and investing in next-generation mobility solutions that are cleaner, smarter, safer, and increasingly connected.
For 25 consecutive years, Hero MotoCorp has remained the world’s largest manufacturer of motorcycles and scooters. Sustaining leadership for a quarter century is not merely a reflection of scale. It is a testament to adaptability, resilience, and enduring customer trust in an industry continuously reshaped by technology, energy transitions, and changing consumer expectations.
Our journey began with a singular mission — to democratise mobility for millions. Today, we are evolving into a diversified mobility and technology enterprise — investing across electric mobility, connected ecosystems, premium segments, advanced R&D, digital platforms, intelligent manufacturing, global partnerships, and sustainable operations.

Long before India became central to global conversations around manufacturing, innovation, and supply chain resilience, Hero MotoCorp was proving that Indian engineering, quality, and operational excellence could compete at the highest level. Today, as the mobility industry undergoes one of the most profound transformations in its history, India is increasingly being recognised not only as a large market, but as a strategic hub for innovation, technology, and resilient manufacturing. Hero MotoCorp is proud to be helping shape that future.
At the same time, we are building a new generation of leadership across businesses, technologies, and markets — combining deep operational experience with fresh thinking, digital capability, and global perspective to lead Hero MotoCorp into its next era of growth.
Reimagining urban mobility through next-generation concepts at EICMA 2025.
Dr. Pawan Munjal
Executive Chairman

That balance has always defined Hero.
I would like to express my heartfelt gratitude to all our stakeholders — customers, employees, dealers, partners, shareholders and communities — for your continued trust and support.
Behind this progress stand the values established by our Founder and Chairman Emeritus, Dr. Brijmohan Lall Munjal — our Hero Forever. He believed that enduring institutions are built not only through ambition, but through trust, humility, consistency, and a deep sense of responsibility. Those values continue to guide our culture and decision- making as we navigate a rapidly changing world.

At Hero MotoCorp, innovation is not pursued for novelty alone. It must ultimately create accessibility, reliability, sustainability, and meaningful value for customers at scale. Behind every milestone at Hero MotoCorp are journeys of million individuals — students commuting to opportunity, entrepreneurs building livelihoods, families seeking reliability, and communities advancing through access to mobility. This human connection remains at the heart of everything we do.
As we look ahead, we remain guided by a simple belief: mobility has the power to transform lives, and progress is most meaningful when it is shared. The future of mobility is being rewritten, and Hero MotoCorp will continue to help lead that future with confidence, responsibility, and purpose.

We are also accelerating investments in artificial Intelligence & digital infrastructure and platforms, data-led decision making, intelligent manufacturing, and emerging technologies that will define the next generation of mobility experiences.
Together, we are helping shape the future of mobility — and Hero MotoCorp will continue to lead that journey with courage, responsibility, and the enduring spirit that has defined us for generations.

CEO’S MESSAGE LEADING THE FUTURE OF MOBILITY
As we build the future of mobility, we continue to invest in R&D for connected technologies, different low emission powertrains and digital capabilities across the value chain.
Dear Shareholders,
I am pleased to share that Hero MotoCorp delivered its highest ever till date annual revenue and profit during FY 2025-26. Revenue from operations grew to ₹ 46,830 crore, reflecting a strong double-digit growth over the previous year, while Profit After Tax rose to ₹ 5,268 crore. EBITDA margins improved to 14.7%, supported by a favourable product mix, premiumisation, cost optimisation and operational efficiencies. The year saw strong momentum across our core motorcycle business, led by both commuter and premium segments. The year demonstrated further dominance of the brand portfolio, led by strong performances from HF Deluxe, Splendor, Xtreme, and Glamour. At the premium end, Harley-Davidson X440T, our product developed through partnership with Harley-Davidson continued to gain traction, with the portfolio registering strong double-digit growth supported by network expansion and brand-led initiatives.

As I write to you for the first time as CEO of Hero MotoCorp, I do so with a deep sense of gratitude, humility and responsibility. It is a privilege to lead an organisation that has shaped the mobility aspirations of millions and remained the industry leader for over 25 years.
Harshavardhan Chitale
CEO, Hero MotoCorp
We also achieved 100% Zero Waste to Landfill operations and enabled 95% product recyclability across the portfolio. Our Gurugram plant received the Platinum Award at the CII National 5S Excellence Competition 2026, and our Tirupati plant earned a GreenCo Gold Rating, recognising our commitment to Zero Waste to Landfill operations and plastic-free facilities. This year, we positively impacted 5.28 lakh beneficiaries through CSR initiatives.
Strategic investments in Euler Motors, continued partnership with Ather Energy and the expansion of our collaboration with Harley-Davidson further reinforced our ambitions across electric mobility and premium segments.
Since joining Hero MotoCorp in January 2026, I have been inspired not only by the strength of our iconic brands, but also by the passion, resilience and commitment of our people. Above all, I have been moved by the enduring trust that millions of customers, partners, investors and stakeholders place in us every day.

Beyond products, we are reimagining the entire mobility experience. Consumers today seek connected, convenient and personalised solutions and our investments in digital platforms, retail transformation and customer engagement are helping us meet these evolving expectations. During the year, we further expanded our premium retail footprint from over 100 touchpoints in FY 2024-25 to 130 touchpoints thereby enhancing accessibility and customer experience across key markets in India.
I would like to express my deepest appreciation to Vikram Kasbekar, Executive Director for his stewardship during the leadership transition as interim CEO and for his continued partnership.
Beyond business, we believe sports represent the relentless pursuit of excellence. Hero MotoCorp strengthened its global impact through partnerships across World Rally-Raid championship, cricket, golf, and hockey. Notably, we supported athletes through the Paralympic Committee of India and the Indian Deaf Cricket Association, reinforcing our commitment to inclusivity and empowerment.

Our scooter business also grew steadily, supported by new launches and improved customer engagement and expansion in urban markets. In scooters, successful launches such as the Destini and Xoom range helped Hero MotoCorp post strong growth significantly strengthening its market position. We remain focused on strengthening our position in this segment through sharper product differentiation and enhanced riding experiences.
I am also deeply grateful to our Executive Chairman, Dr. Pawan Munjal, whose vision and unwavering commitment have shaped Hero MotoCorp into the industry-leading institution. His guidance continues to inspire us as we continue to build the next chapter of mobility.
Our Company also accelerated its global expansion strategy with strong momentum across South Asia, Latin America, Africa and Europe. International business recorded robust growth driven by strong demand for products such as the Hunk 125R, Hunk 160R and Hunter series. During the year, Hero MotoCorp announced its entry into key European markets including Germany, Italy, France, Spain and the UK, supported by Euro5+ compliant products, strategic distributor partnerships and an expanding premium and electric vehicle portfolio.

I would like to thank our customers, dealer partners, supply chain partners and investors for their continued trust. Most importantly, I thank every member of the Hero MotoCorp family for their dedication and passion to drive our progress and define our culture.
FY 2025-26 has been a defining year for Hero MotoCorp as we reinforced our leadership position while accelerating our transformation into a future-ready mobility company. In a rapidly evolving mobility landscape, our focus remained clear - delivering profitable growth, strengthening our core business, investing in future technologies and building mobility solutions that are sustainable, innovative and globally relevant. Over the course of the year, we made significant progress across premiumisation, electric mobility, global expansion, digital transformation and operational excellence while continuing to stay deeply connected to the evolving aspirations of our customers and communities.

VIDA, our electric mobility business, delivered a landmark year with record year-on-year retail growth of 190%. We introduced the 'EVOOTER' category with the launch of the VIDA VX2 and debuted our first young riders, electric vehicle (first of its kind in India) Dirt.E K3 at EICMA 2025. We are building a comprehensive ecosystem for electric vehicles, charging infrastructure, and Battery-as-a-Service offerings to grow rapidly and gain share in electric mobility.
As we move ahead, we remain focused on strengthening our core business, accelerating growth in premium and electric mobility, expanding our global footprint and building a more agile, future-ready organisation. Backed by strong fundamentals and a clear strategic roadmap, we are confident about the growth ahead.
Sustainability remained a core pillar of our strategy. We advanced climate action by increasing our renewable energy share to 32% and maintaining 500% water positivity.
As we build the future of mobility, we continue to invest in R&D for connected technologies, different low emission powertrains and digital capabilities across the value chain.

Carbon Offsets

Haridwar Plant
Cooling towers are critical to continuous plant operations, supporting heat rejection for compressors, chillers, and other process equipment at the Halol plant’s utility centre. However, legacy high-inertia cast-metal fans led to elevated energy consumption, inefficient airflow, and increased mechanical wear. Transitioning to composite fibre fans enabled optimisation of the cooling cycle, reducing power demand and improving overall utility efficiency.

Optimising thermal energy is a key focus area in our energy conservation strategy. Historically, low-grade waste heat from engine assembly chillers was rejected into the atmosphere, while thermal processes remained heavily dependent on fossil fuels, increasing Scope 1 emissions.

Governed by Integrity
Our Governance Framework
Business Ethics

Business Ethics
At the core of our corporate governance approach is a robust, well-structured framework led by a diverse and experienced Board of Directors comprising of Executive and Non-Executive members. Our Board is supported by specialised committees that bring deep expertise to guide our strategic direction and oversee operations. We emphasise diversity across the Board and organisation, while remaining aligned with evolving legal and regulatory requirements. Our policies are reviewed at least once every three years to ensure continued relevance and reinforce our commitment to transparency, accountability, and sound governance.
Upholding business ethics and integrity is fundamental to building a responsible business and reflects our commitment to achieving success transparently and ethically. We adhere to the highest standards of business conduct in line with applicable laws, regulations, and ethical principles. Ethical behaviour is embedded in our culture, with a strong focus on transparency, accountability, and fairness across all interactions, fostering a trustworthy and respectful work environment. Employees are expected to uphold the highest standards of integrity, guided by a robust Code of Conduct that promotes honesty, sustainability, and social responsibility.

Integrity anchors our governance approach, driving ethical conduct, transparency, and accountability across operations while reinforcing trust and ensuring responsible, compliant decision-making at every level.
Code of Conduct
Whistleblower/Vigil Mechanism
We embed integrity and compliance into our day-to- day operations through strict adherence to our Code of Conduct (CoC). All employees are required to complete mandatory CoC training, formally commit to the Code, and demonstrate appropriate conduct. During the year, 100% of employees completed the annual sign-off, reaffirming their understanding of and compliance with the CoC.

We uphold the highest ethical standards through a robust vigilance mechanism in compliance with the Companies Act, 2013 and SEBI Regulations, 2015, enabling stakeholders, including employees, directors, vendors, and suppliers, to report concerns related to unethical behaviour, fraud, or Code of Conduct (CoC) violations. Our Whistleblower Policy, aligned with the Companies Act and SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, ensures protection and confidential reporting through a toll-free number, email, and web-based hotline, without fear of retaliation. The Ethics Committee oversees the mechanism, providing secure channels, including a third-party managed Ethics Helpline and Protected Disclosures, and ensures all complaints are investigated and regularly reported to the Audit Committee.
 Read more on our CoC here: Hero MotoCorp Code of Conduct
Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption (ABAC)

Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption (ABAC)
We strictly prohibit all forms of bribery and corruption, ensuring fair and transparent business practices. An organisation-wide ABAC risk assessment, conducted by an independent third party across operations in India, Germany, Bangladesh, and Colombia, identified government touchpoints, benchmarked processes against Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, UK Bribery Act, and Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) guidelines, and highlighted areas for improvement, including policy enhancements, process changes, and stakeholder awareness. Based on the findings, we established a comprehensive ABAC framework with management oversight, strengthened internal policies released a formal ABAC policy, and a Supplier Code of Conduct, supported by periodic monitoring. ABAC remains a key pillar of our compliance framework.
HMCL has a standalone Vigil Mechanism/Whistleblower Policy which is also incorporated within the Code of Conduct. The awareness and enforcement of the Vigil Mechanism Policy is disseminated to all employees through multiple channels including the mandatory Code of Conduct Training Programme.

Governance & Information Security Oversight
We adopt a proactive approach to managing vulnerabilities across IT systems, networks and applications, supported by defined Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for servers, workstations and business applications. The global trade architecture has entered a period of substantial reorientation following the commencement of Trump 2.0 administration. For the automotive sector, the operating environment has been particularly volatile; with the repeal of EV-linked tax credits and the threat of bilateral tariff escalations. Even the World Trade Organization (WTO) recently flagged downside risks to global trade due to rising protectionist policies. Moreover, the conflict in West Asia has compelled OEMs to re-work their cost arithmetic; which had already been facing pressures owing to supply constraints with regards to Heavy Rare Earth Elements (HREs).

Back-Ended Growth in the EV Industry
Beyond the ongoing electrification of scooters, a defining trend over the last four years has been the outperformance of ICE scooters within the two-wheeler market. The ICE scooter industry expanded at a 15% CAGR from FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26, higher than the 12% growth of the broader ICE two-wheeler market. Consequently, the share of ICE scooters within the ICE two-wheeler sector rose from 30% in FY 2021-22 to 34% in FY 2025-26, propelled by structural and demographic shifts across India.

In FY 2025-26, electric two-wheeler retails grew by 21% YoY to 1.46 million units, a trajectory largely in-line with the previous year. While the pace appeared steady for most of the fiscal year, the bulk of this growth was concentrated in March due to the anticipated rollback of the PM E-DRIVE subsidy—which was eventually extended to July 2026—and the West Asia conflict, which accelerated the shift toward EV adoption. Consequently, this strong performance in March pushed the final EV adoption rate to 6.6%, up from the 6.2% recorded in the prior year.
Supply Issues in the EV Industry Due to Heavy Rare Earth Magnet Shortage
Hero MotoCorp has successfully mitigated the risk by moving to Light Rare Earth (Non-restricted) & Bonded Magnets, procuring Sub Assemblies from China and finding alternate supply routes—including free zone geographic locations like Vietnam & Europe—before fully switching over to ferrite magnets. These actions coupled with timely intervention in supply chain solutions, ensured that the Company did not lose any production commitment in FY 2025-26.

Growth in the EV segment was significantly challenged during the reporting period owing to a global shortage of Heavy Rare Earth Elements (HREE), a critical component for high-efficiency electric motors. This disruption was precipitated in late 2025 by China, which controls over 90% of global HREE production, introducing a stringent export licensing regime. The new mandate required manufacturers to provide exhaustive end-use declarations, extending export clearance timelines from a few days to a protracted 45-60 days. This bottleneck effectively paralysed the ‘just-in-time’ supply chains upon which Indian EV manufacturers heavily relied on.

COMPLIANCE WITH SECRETARIAL STANDARDS

COMPLIANCE WITH SECRETARIAL STANDARDS
The Company has developed and maintains its own in-house SDD without procuring or integrating any external software or tool from third-party vendors. The database along with its server is entirely hosted and secured within the Company’s internal IT ecosystem, ensuring that no sensitive information flows outside the organisation. SDD is seamlessly integrated with the internal systems enabling the automatic identification and recognition of Designated Persons (DPs) according to the criteria established in the code. All unpublished price sensitive data shared, internally or externally, are recorded in the SDD and a notice is concurrently shared informing the recipient to maintain confidentiality and refrain from trading in the securities of the Company. At the end of each quarter, confirmations are obtained from respective functional heads or SPOCs to confirm whether any UPSI was generated during the quarter and if so, whether requisite details have been entered into the SDD and the notice has been issued to the recipient. Further, pre-clearance applications and their corresponding approvals are also processed directly through the SDD. Annual/half-yearly disclosures from DPs, intimations of closure of trading window and all other necessary information/reports are maintained in the SDD. The SDD is access restricted and governed by a justification- based access protocol. Any user attempting to access the database must provide a valid reason, which is recorded automatically within the SDD. The system maintains a complete audit trail of all entries and modifications, enabling transparent monitoring and future inspection by auditors.

 Hero MotoCorp Ltd. has implemented a comprehensive road safety ecosystem aligned with SDG 3.6 through four key initiatives: Be a Hero, Traffic Training Parks, Helmet Distribution Drive, and Surakshit Aatmanirbhar Bharat, focused on awareness, skill development, and behavioural change among students, commuters, and informal workers. A mixed- method approach was used for Traffic Training Parks and Helmet Distribution, while the other two relied on qualitative insights. The Traffic Training Parks improved practical riding skills such as balance, braking, turning, and lane discipline through simulator and live training, with high engagement and consistent attendance across all locations. The Helmet Distribution Drive provided 6,000 ISI-certified helmets, with 90%+ engagement, 91% satisfaction, and 97% awareness of helmet importance, though consistent compliance (especially pillion use) remained partial. The Be a Hero campaign reached over 250 schools and colleges, generating 250,000+ safety pledges and improving awareness of traffic rules and helmet/ seatbelt use. The Surakshit Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative distributed 6,000 helmets and 6,000 reflective jackets, reaching millions through 50+ million digital impressions and significantly improving safety awareness and intended behaviour among vulnerable riders.
Project 2: Farm Ponds (Water Conservation Initiative, Rajasthan):

Project 2: Farm Ponds (Water Conservation Initiative, Rajasthan):
 The Farm Pond Project started in April 2023 serving 62 farmers in Dausa, has proven highly relevant in addressing water scarcity, with 98% previously facing shortages. Aligned with initiatives like Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) and Atal Bhujal Yojana, the project improved water access for 92% of farmers, increased crop yields (37.9% for wheat and 68.1% for pulses), and nearly doubled annual incomes from H 32,960 to H 59,900, while boosting crop intensity from 32.25% to 91.58%. Efficiency gains included reduced irrigation time (over 5 hours to under 1 hour for 56% of farmers), though issues like pond lining and weak local institutional involvement persisted. Broader impacts included reduced migration, improved livelihoods, and knowledge sharing (84% farmers spreading practices), along with environmental benefits such as better soil moisture retention, though limited tree plantation participation (24%) constrained ecological outcomes. The project demonstrates strong effectiveness and scalability potential, with opportunities to enhance sustainability through better technical support, community engagement, gender inclusion, and institutional strengthening.

Project 5: Shiksha (Scholarship Support & HERO ASHA Centres):
Project Shiksha, funded by Hero MotoCorp Ltd., improves access to quality education for underprivileged students through scholarships at BML Munjal University and remedial learning via HERO ASHA Education Centres. At BMU, 50 students receive financial support (86% tuition waivers, 12% full coverage), with 88% reporting reduced financial burden and 66% showing notable academic improvement; infrastructure upgrades such as hostels, smart classrooms, and labs are widely recognised (98% awareness, 92% satisfaction), though hostel satisfaction remains mixed. The programme also reports a strong 90% placement rate, with graduates earning ₹50,000–₹1,00,000 per month, reflecting improved employability and socio-economic mobility. The HERO ASHA Centres operate across 280 centres in locations including Dharuhera, Neemrana, Haridwar, and Jaipur, supporting over 13,000 students (Grades 3–8). Evaluation findings show that 74% of students report significant learning improvement and 26% report moderate gains, along with improved attendance and reduced dropout rates. Foundational learning outcomes have also strengthened, with mathematics progression reaching division-level proficiency in over 70% of higher-grade students and reading fluency achieved by 70–87% of students in Classes 6–8. Project Shiksha demonstrates strong academic and social impact, supported by improving employability outcomes and emerging sustainability through alumni engagement and diversified funding.

 The “Be A Sporting Hero” initiative by Hero MotoCorp Ltd. (April 2023–March 2024) strengthened India’s inclusive sports ecosystem through four targeted programmes. Project Khelo in rural Jhajjar engaged 20 youth (55% girls, ages 12–18), with 65% reporting excellent fitness and 55% highest self-confidence, and the girls’ team finishing runner-up in Haryana Football Premier League; the Deaf Cricket Development Programme trained 30 deaf athletes (50% female), where 100% played competitive matches for the first time, 50% were scouted for Deaf Premier League- level opportunities, and 40% for national competitions; the Hero Para-Athlete Programme across 10 states saw 90% of participants improve performance and 85% enhance mental resilience through holistic support; and the Mary Kom Regional Boxing Development Initiative, led by Mary Kom, improved technical skills, confidence, and competitive exposure for female boxers. The initiatives highlight strong gender inclusion, grassroots impact, and measurable physical and psychosocial gains, while pointing to ongoing challenges in accessibility, infrastructure, and sustainable career pathways.

These vehicles are subsequently sent to a Registered Vehicle Scrapping Facility (RVSF), where they are dismantled and the various types of waste are segregated. Regarding plastic waste, all post-consumer plastic packaging waste is collected and safely disposed off through authorised Plastic Waste Processors. Furthermore, any plastic waste segregated at the RVSF is disposed of through authorised plastic waste recyclers.

AI-based safety capturing is no longer just a "futuristic concept"—it is a core driver of financial and operational resilience by shifting from reactive (learning from accidents) to predictive (preventing them before they happen). At Hero MotoCorp, Hazard identification is done through a structured and documented procedure namely Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) where all the risks of a particular section are captured and assessed. Hazards are categorised into Physical, Mechanical, Electrical, Chemical, Biological and Others. The main element of HIRA is to identify all materials, agents, conditions or activities with the potential to cause injury or illness, damage to the business and its property. While carrying out Hazard Assessment, all the activities in each section are selected to identify the significant risks. For all the significant risks, control measures are defined to mitigate the risks as per the hierarchy of safety controls. More focus is given on elimination of Hazards and engineering controls. We have the integration of advanced AI and IoT-based solutions to monitor and mitigate unsafe practices and behaviour on the shop floor in real-time. AI-based safety capturing is no longer just a "futuristic concept" – it is a core driver of financial and operational resilience by shifting from reactive (learning from accidents) to predictive (preventing them before they happen).

8. Does the entity have any project related to reducing Green House Gas emission? If yes, then provide details.
In FY 26, Hero MotoCorp made a strategic shift in hazardous waste management. An initiative to transition from co-processing of paint sludge to a recycle & reuse model by partnering with the recycling facility, the initiative helped in diversion of 28% of paint sludge waste from traditional co-processing to be converted into functional industrial primer.

Yes, total 123 projects across various plants have been taken to reduce Green House Gas emission and to improve the energy efficiency in the plants. Some of the major energy conservation projects are listed as follows: (i) Euler Power consumption reduction of dual tone production at paint shop (ii) Energy saving in steel phase identified induction motors (iii) Replacement of existing (star delta based) air compressor of 733 CFM capacity with new compressor of 563 CFM having VFD control. (iv) Reduce energy consumption of Compressed Air Handling system (v) Control of individual lines of compressed air supply across shops and for main incoming air supply during non - production hours (vi) Process control initiatives in the paint shops (vii) HPFC panel reconditioning for power factor improvement (vii) Replacement of non efficient compressor with energy efficient new compressors (viii) Solar concentrator for canteen area (ix) adiabatic cooling systems to optimise power consumption (x) Reduction of energy consumption by resising of pumps of cooling tower along with VFD provision total energy saving through all projects is approximately 61 lakh kWh.

10. Briefly describe the waste management practices adopted in your establishments. Describe the strategy adopted by your company to reduce usage of hazardous and toxic chemicals in your products and processes and the practices adopted to manage such wastes.
Hero MotoCorp have a robust mechanism of waste management which promotes reducing its waste at the source, promoting sustainable packaging and adopting method to utilise waste as resource for others i.e. co-processing in cement industries. Another such example is upcycling of grinding sludge which is converted to ferric alum & paint sludge into functional industrial primer which becomes useful resources to other industries. We have also adopted innovative technologies to eliminate process waste i.e. introduction of water-based painting which creates zero VOC's, zero paint sludge and low water consumption. The Company also embarked upon the journey of Zero Waste to Landfill from 2018- 19 to 2025-26 where all our plants are certified as Zero Waste to Landfill. Elimination of single use plastic was another initiative where all our plants were certified as "Single Use Plastic Free" Plants.

Meaning of Internal Financial Controls with reference to standalone financial statements
A company's internal financial control with reference to standalone financial statements is a process designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A company's internal financial control with reference to standalone financial statements includes those policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company are being made only in accordance with authorisations of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorised acquisition, use, or disposition of the company's assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.

3.20 Contingent liabilities and contingent assets

3.20 Contingent liabilities and contingent assets
A contingent liability exists when there is a possible but not probable obligation, or a present obligation that may, but probably will not, require an outflow of resources, or a present obligation whose amount cannot be estimated reliably. Contingent liabilities do not warrant provisions, but are disclosed unless the possibility of outflow of resources is remote. Contingent assets are neither recognised nor disclosed in the standalone financial statements. However, contingent assets are assessed continually and if it is virtually certain that an inflow of economic benefits will arise, the asset and related income are recognised in the period in which the change occurs.

Ind AS 12, International Tax Reform – Pillar Two Model Rules applicable immediately - The amendments provide a temporary mandatory relief from deferred tax accounting for top-up tax and require companies to disclose that they have applied the relief. This relief is immediate and applies retrospectively. The amendments also require companies to provide new disclosures to compensate for potential loss of information resulting from the relief. Such disclosures are to be provided for annual reporting periods beginning on or after April 1, 2025. The Company has reviewed the amendment and based on its evaluation has determined that it does not have any impact in its financial statements.
(b) Defined benefit plans
The cost of the defined benefit plan and other post-employment benefits and the present value of such obligation are determined using actuarial valuations. An actuarial valuation involves making various assumptions that may differ from actual developments in the future. These include the determination of the discount rate, future salary increases, mortality rates and future pension increases. Due to the complexities involved in the valuation and its long-term nature, a defined benefit obligation is sensitive to changes in these assumptions. All assumptions are reviewed at each reporting date.

Employee Stock Option Plan
The Employee Stock Options Scheme titled “Employee Incentive Scheme 2014 - Options and Restricted Stock Unit” hereafter referred to as “Employee Incentive Scheme 2014” or “the Scheme” was approved by the shareholders of the Company through postal ballot on September 22, 2014. The Scheme covered 49,90,000 options/restricted units for 49,90,000 equity shares. The Scheme allows the issue of options/restricted stock units (RSU)/performance linked restricted stock units (PRSU) to employees of the Company which are convertible to one equity share of the Company. As per the Scheme, the Nomination and Remuneration Committee grants the Options/RSU/PRSU to the employees deemed eligible. The options and RSU/PRSU granted vest over a period of 4 and 3 years respectively from the date of the grant in proportions specified in the respective ESOP Plans. The fair value as on the date of the grant of the options/RSU/PRSU, representing Stock compensation charge, is expensed over the vesting period.

The Company manages its capital to ensure that the Company will be able to continue as a going concern while maximising the return to stakeholders through efficient allocation of capital towards expansion of business, optimisation of working capital requirements and deployment of surplus funds into various investment options. The following is the basis of categorising the financial instruments measured at fair value into Level 1 to Level 3:
Level 1: This level includes financial assets that are measured by reference to quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.
Level 2: This level includes financial assets and liabilities, measured using inputs other than quoted prices included within Level 1 that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly (i.e., as prices) or indirectly (i.e., derived from prices).

Level 2: This level includes financial assets and liabilities, measured using inputs other than quoted prices included within Level 1 that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly (i.e., as prices) or indirectly (i.e., derived from prices).

A contingent liability exists when there is a possible but not probable obligation, or a present obligation that may, but probably will not, require an outflow of resources, or a present obligation whose amount cannot be estimated reliably. Contingent liabilities do not warrant provisions, but are disclosed unless the possibility of outflow of resources is remote. Contingent assets are neither recognised nor disclosed in the financial statements. However, contingent assets are assessed continually and if it is virtually certain that an inflow of economic benefits will arise, the asset and related income are recognised in the period in which the change occurs.

ESG Leadership and Corporate Citizenship

ESG Leadership and Corporate Citizenship
The re-appointment of Dr. Munjal is also a vote for the Company’s leadership in Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) standards. Under his guidance, the Company has become the only Indian two-wheeler manufacturer listed on the Dow Jones Sustainability Index (DJSI).
These recognitions reflect a leader who is not only respected within the Indian industry but is also a "Global Statesman of Mobility". His roles in the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) and the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM) have allowed him to shape the industry's roadmap, ensuring that Hero MotoCorp remains at the forefront of policy and technological shifts.
Sustainability and CSR Impact

Sustainability and CSR Impact
The re-appointment of Dr. Pawan Munjal for a five-year term commencing October 1, 2026 is, therefore, a strategic imperative. His continued leadership provides the stability and execution continuity required to successfully complete the ongoing transformation and to position the Company for its next phase of growth across global, electric, and premium mobility segments. The Board is of the considered view that this continuity is critical to sustaining momentum and fully realising the value of the Company’s strategic investments. Members are accordingly encouraged to vote in favor of the proposed re-appointment in the long-term interests of the Company and its stakeholders.
Dr. Munjal’s inclusion in the 2025 TIME100 Climate list highlights his role as a global leader in advancing business climate action.

• CSR Reach: In FY 2024-25 and FY 2025-26, CSR initiatives reached over 1.3 million beneficiaries across India. Over the last decade, the Company’s flagship road safety initiatives have reached over 1.6 million individuals, promoting safer riding behaviour, responsible mobility and road safety awareness. .
Performance Evaluation

Performance Evaluation
The Board of Directors highly commends Dr. Munjal's effective leadership, noting his exceptional ability to maintain a balanced role, seamlessly managing corporate governance responsibilities as Chair while providing executive guidance to the organisation. His engagement with the Board is consistently constructive and productive, marked by his respect for colleagues' viewpoints and active solicitation of ideas and suggestions. Furthermore, the Board recognises Dr. Pawan Munjal as the Company’s best Brand Ambassador. Dr. Munjal has successfully led the Company and the Board to ensure the organisation is future-ready and already positioned on the right strategic path. Looking ahead, the Board supports Dr. Munjal’s planned evolution of his role to focus more intensively on high-level strategic areas, allowing Mr. Harshavardhan Chitale, Chief Executive Officer to manage day-to-day operations. Key strategic priorities under Dr. Pawan Munjal’s guidance will include fostering cultural alignment, addressing succession planning, strengthening the senior leadership team, and driving aggressive growth in the EV portfolio. His continued oversight will also ensure the new Chief Executive Officer and leadership team are fully supported during the initial transition period. The Directors affirm that Dr. Pawan Munjal's contributions are vital to the Company's continued success, demonstrating effective leadership necessary for the next phase of growth.

• Diversity: The Company has committed to achieving 30% gender diversity by 2030, with meaningful progress already evident- reflected in 30% representation at the Board level and 40% across senior leadership.
These initiatives are not just social obligations but are core to the brand’s "Nation First" identity, which Dr. Munjal has cultivated as a key competitive differentiator.

The global business community’s recognition of Dr. Pawan Munjal’s leadership provides an objective measure of his strategic caliber. His awards during the 2021-2026 period span corporate leadership, innovation, and social impact.
